svg.desc: candidate number: 40; slug: self-funded-health,-pbm-&-workers'-comp-arbitrage; title: Self-Funded Health, PBM & Workers' Comp Arbitrage; category: Employee benefits & E-Mod brokerage; production stage: approved_master; scores: revenue potential: 25; profit margin potential: 24; team efficiency: 19; startup accessibility: 13; automation potential: 12; dimension max: revenue potential: 25; profit margin potential: 25; team efficiency: 20; startup accessibility: 15; automation potential: 15; total score: 93; tier label: Elite Small-Team Cash Machine; evidence confidence: High; uncertainty band: ±3 pts; uncertainty bounds: low: 90; high: 96; uncertainty note: Editorial sensitivity band, not a statistical interval. Confidence is a supplied classification; independent source review is required.; score rationale: revenue potential: Revenue Potential: 25/25. Form 5500 renewal targeting, CAA 2021 fiduciary fee-disclosure wedges, level-funded/captive ERISA transitions, pass-through PBMs, and Workers' Comp NCCI E-Mod audits generate $40–$65 PEPM evergreen annuities.; profit margin potential: Profit Margin Potential: 24/25. Form 5500 renewal targeting, CAA 2021 fiduciary fee-disclosure wedges, level-funded/captive ERISA transitions, pass-through PBMs, and Workers' Comp NCCI E-Mod audits generate $40–$65 PEPM evergreen annuities.; team efficiency: Team Efficiency: 19/20. Form 5500 renewal targeting, CAA 2021 fiduciary fee-disclosure wedges, level-funded/captive ERISA transitions, pass-through PBMs, and Workers' Comp NCCI E-Mod audits generate $40–$65 PEPM evergreen annuities.; automation potential: Automation Potential: 12/15. Form 5500 renewal targeting, CAA 2021 fiduciary fee-disclosure wedges, level-funded/captive ERISA transitions, pass-through PBMs, and Workers' Comp NCCI E-Mod audits generate $40–$65 PEPM evergreen annuities.; economics: gross revenue range: $120,000–$950,000 USD annually; retained revenue range: $120,000–$950,000 USD annually; retained share: 1.0; net profit margin range: 32–58%; retained profit margin range: 32–58%; owner net profit potential: $38,400–$551,000 USD annually, before personal taxes and reinvestment; startup capital range: $8,000–$45,000 USD; monthly opex range: $2,000–$11,000 USD; time to first deal: 2–5 months; automation coverage: 0.82; typical team size: full time including owner: 1; contractors: 3; total people: 4; includes contractors note: Headcount includes the working owner and recurring contractors as people, not FTE equivalents. Contractors may be part-time. Scaled scenario adds one employee and one contractor; external vendor workforces are not counted as internal team members.; revenue basis: Net retained PEPM benefits advisory fees, stop-loss/TPA commissions, and contingent Workers' Comp E-Mod refund splits; excludes employer claim funds and insurance premiums; cost basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; automation levers: Form 5500 Schedule A/C renewal scraper; NADAC vs spread-PBM repricing engine; NCCI E-Mod & payroll-code audit analyzer; key risks: Incumbent broker defense at renewal; Stop-loss laser or shock-claim volatility; State insurance producer & TPA licensing; regulatory notes: Hold active state Life & Health and Property & Casualty producer licenses and deliver full ERISA §408(b)(2) / CAA 2021 compensation disclosures.; Structure stop-loss specific/aggregate attachment points, run-out coverage, and RBP balance-bill legal defense cleanly.; track ids: track_1; track_2; track labels: Asymmetric & Data-Arbitrage Plays; Grey-Zone Growth & Traffic Arbitrage; plays: id: erisa_level_funded_transparent_pbm_bor_arbitrage; inputs: Public Form 5500 filings and available Schedule A/C records, employer size and plan-year information, employer-confirmed renewal dates and appropriately obtained business contact details.; Employer authorization, incumbent fee disclosures, plan documents, aggregate claims and pharmacy reports, stop-loss terms, underwriting requirements and privacy-controlled access to necessary participant information.; Licensed broker and specialist relationships, TPA and stop-loss proposals, captive participation terms, PBM rebate and spread definitions, NADAC availability and fallback pricing rules, and a $40–$65 PEPM service proposal.; mechanism: Use public Form 5500 Schedule A/C information, where filed and informative, to identify mid-market renewal and compensation-review opportunities, then offer an employer-authorized CAA 2021 service-provider fee-disclosure review. A properly licensed advisory team can seek broker-of-record appointments and compare bundled coverage with separately contracted TPA, stop-loss or suitable captive arrangements and a transparent pass-through PBM using an explicitly defined NADAC-based pricing methodology. Negotiate recurring $40–$65 PEPM advisory fees where supported by scope and client agreement, with all commissions and indirect compensation disclosed and no assumption that unbundling guarantees savings.; metrics: Recurring advisory revenue: enrolled employees multiplied by the contracted $40–$65 PEPM fee, less servicing costs and disclosed fee offsets.; Risk-adjusted employer cost: claims, administration, stop-loss premiums, pharmacy costs, collateral and runout obligations minus realized rebates and recoveries.; Service and retention quality: renewal retention, disclosure completeness, pharmacy guarantee reconciliation variance and unresolved participant access issues.; name: Mid-Market Level-Funded Benefits and Transparent PBM Advisory Operator; platform risks: detection metric: Adverse-scenario funding gap, claims-to-budget variance, unrecovered stop-loss balances and unexplained differences between disclosed and received compensation.; failure mode: The proposed unbundled plan produces adverse claims exposure or undisclosed compensation despite appearing cheaper on headline premiums.; fallback: Retain or competitively rebid the existing structure when risk-adjusted economics are unfavorable, obtain explicit pricing fallbacks and narrow the engagement to disclosed advisory work until implementation conditions are satisfied.; impact: Employer costs exceed projections, coverage continuity deteriorates and advisory fees or the BOR relationship become disputed.; trigger: Incomplete claims data, stop-loss lasers or exclusions, nonrefundable captive collateral, ambiguous PBM rebate definitions or unsupported NADAC pricing for uncovered products.; track id: track_1; workflow: 1. Analyze publicly available filings through permitted access methods, identify likely renewal opportunities and confirm current plan arrangements directly because filings are historical and may omit relevant compensation details.; 2. Obtain employer authorization, review applicable CAA 2021 disclosures and existing termination terms, and define advisory deliverables and compensation before requesting any BOR appointment.; 3. Compare fully insured and level-funded options using expected and adverse claims scenarios, stop-loss exclusions and lasers, captive collateral, TPA fees, pharmacy guarantees and rebates actually retained by the employer.; 4. Implement the employer-selected structure with licensed parties, privacy safeguards and continuity planning; collect agreed PEPM fees and review total costs, disclosures and service performance at each renewal.; id: workers_comp_ncci_emod_retroactive_recovery; inputs: Customer authorization, three to four years of policies and premium audits, payroll registers, job-duty evidence, overtime breakdowns, officer election documents and subcontractor coverage records.; Applicable state classification rules, NCCI or independent-bureau worksheets, experience-period and valuation dates, carrier loss runs and documented claim corrections.; Carrier and bureau dispute procedures, policy-specific correction deadlines, a 30%–40% realized-refund agreement and licensed brokerage support for any BOR renewal engagement.; mechanism: Audit three to four historical policy years where carrier, state and rating-bureau correction rules permit, checking actual duties, payroll classifications, eligible overtime adjustments and officer exclusions or limits. Reconcile NCCI experience-rating worksheets, or the applicable independent bureau's equivalent, to accurate carrier loss reports and valuation dates; an open reserve is not an error merely because the ultimate claim later costs less. Recover documented premium overpayments for a negotiated 30%–40% contingency and pursue separately authorized, properly licensed BOR renewal work.; metrics: Realized premium recovery: received refunds and usable policy credits divided by audited historical premium, segmented by payroll, classification and experience-mod correction.; Correction conversion: dollars recovered divided by dollars submitted, alongside days from supported dispute to revised audit or bureau worksheet.; Renewal economics: separately disclosed brokerage revenue and verified prospective premium effect, controlling for payroll, operations, rates and coverage changes.; name: Workers' Compensation Classification and Experience-Mod Recovery Operator; platform risks: detection metric: Rejected correction dollars by reason, percentage of payroll supported by contemporaneous records and net premium change after the full audit.; failure mode: A carrier or rating bureau rejects proposed corrections because classifications, loss valuations or retroactive deadlines were misinterpreted.; fallback: Withdraw unsupported claims, disclose any additional premium exposure, use the bureau's documented dispute process for defensible items and improve prospective payroll and claims reporting.; impact: No refund is issued, advisory effort is unrecovered and a broader audit may identify additional premium owed.; trigger: Unsupported separation of payroll, missing officer elections, treatment of later reserve reductions as historical errors or submission outside the permitted correction period.; track id: track_1; workflow: 1. Map each policy to its governing state and bureau rules, establish the allowable correction window and reconcile audited payroll to contemporaneous employment and job-duty records.; 2. Test class-code assignments, permitted overtime premium exclusions, officer elections or payroll limits and subcontractor treatment without relabeling work merely to obtain a cheaper rate.; 3. Reconcile experience-mod inputs against losses reported for the applicable valuation date; submit evidenced payroll, classification or loss-data corrections to the carrier and bureau as required.; 4. Obtain revised audits or rating worksheets, trace resulting premium credits through endorsements and receipts, collect the 30%–40% contingency and separately quote licensed BOR renewal services.; id: erisa_self_funded_specialty_drug_importation_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: Employer Self-Funded ERISA Plan International Specialty-Drug Importation Arbitrage; mechanism: Contracting with mid-market US employers (100–5,000 employees) operating self-funded ERISA health plans to carve out high-cost specialty biologics and GLP-1s ($6,000–$15,000/mo US PBM list price) and source the identical manufacturer-sealed drugs from licensed Tier-1 pharmacies in Canada, the UK, Australia, and New Zealand at $800–$2,200/mo—waiving the employee's copay to $0 while taking 25–35% of the employer's $50,000–$100,000/yr per-patient savings.; inputs: Department of Labor (DOL) Form 5500 Schedule A/C database identifying self-funded ERISA employers by broker, TPA, and stop-loss carrier; Licensed international pharmacy dispensation network across Tier-1 jurisdictions (Canada, UK, Australia, New Zealand) with cold-chain courier logistics; Turnkey ERISA Summary Plan Description (SPD) 'Specialty Drug Carve-Out Amendment' and $0-copay patient concierge portal; workflow: Mine DOL Form 5500 filings to target CFOs and benefits directors of self-funded companies with 150–3,000 covered lives; Audit the employer's anonymized pharmacy claims file to flag the 1–3% of members driving 45–60% of total drug spend (Humira, Stelara, Skyrizi, Dupixent, Enbrel, Ozempic); Plug in a voluntary $0-copay international personal-importation program alongside the existing TPA, fulfilling 90-day cold-chain prescriptions at 60–80% below US PBM prices; Bill the self-funded employer plan a shared-savings contingency fee equal to 25–35% of verified net claim reduction ($15,000–$30,000/yr per enrolled specialty patient); metrics: Verified annual specialty-claim savings ($) per self-funded employer group; Net shared-savings fee revenue ($15k–$30k/yr) per enrolled specialty patient; Employee $0-copay opt-in conversion rate (target: >85%); platform risks: failure mode: Incumbent PBM rebate-contract retaliation or cold-chain customs shipment delay; trigger: Legacy PBM threatening to withhold formulary rebates if specialty scripts are carved out, or border clearance delays on temperature-sensitive biologics; impact: Delayed employer onboarding or need for local emergency bridge fills; detection metric: Cold-chain transit temperature telemetry and net employer savings after accounting for any forfeited PBM rebates; fallback: Target independent TPAs and transparent pass-through PBMs first, combine international sourcing with US Manufacturer Patient Assistance Program (PAP) optimization, and maintain domestic bridge-fill coverage; id: section_340b_contract_pharmacy_spread_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: 340B Contract-Pharmacy & Covered-Entity Drug Price Spread Arbitrage; mechanism: Partnering with HRSA-qualified 340B Covered Entities (Federally Qualified Health Centers, Ryan White clinics, disproportionate-share rural hospitals) to provide turnkey Third-Party Administrator (TPA) split-billing software, specialty contract-pharmacy fulfillment, and tele-referral capture—buying outpatient specialty medications at 25–50%+ statutory 340B discounts while collecting 100% full commercial insurance reimbursement and splitting the multi-thousand-dollar per-script margin via compliant flat administrative/dispensing fees.; inputs: HRSA OPAIS (Office of Pharmacy Affairs Information System) database of Covered Entities and registered contract pharmacies; 340B split-billing / virtual-inventory accumulator software tracking 11-digit NDCs, prescriber NPIs, and patient-eligibility encounters; Licensed specialty/mail-order contract pharmacy network and commercial payer PBMs; workflow: Identify under-monetized 340B Covered Entities (FQHCs, grantees, rural hospitals) with low specialty capture rates in the HRSA OPAIS registry; Deploy split-billing TPA software and mail-order specialty contract-pharmacy infrastructure that captures commercially insured prescriptions written or co-managed by clinic providers; Reimburse the pharmacy at full commercial payer rates ($3,000–$12,000/script) while replenishing drug inventory via the clinic's 340B wholesaler account at $800–$4,000/script; Charge fixed fair-market-value per-dispense administrative, software, and clinical-management fees that capture a major share of the net spread while funding the clinic's safety-net mission; metrics: Captured commercially insured 340B scripts per month per Covered Entity; Gross commercial-to-340B acquisition spread ($1,500–$6,000+) per specialty fill; HRSA audit pass rate (zero duplicate Medicaid discount or diversion findings); platform risks: failure mode: Manufacturer contract-pharmacy restriction policies or HRSA 'patient definition' audit findings; trigger: Drug manufacturers restricting 340B replenishment to a single contract pharmacy unless claims data is submitted, or filling scripts for patients without a documented clinic encounter; impact: Loss of 340B ceiling price on specific NDCs or HRSA repayment liability; detection metric: 100% EHR encounter-to-NPI match verification prior to 340B replenishment accumulation and automated ESP (340B ESP) data submission; fallback: Operate an in-house entity-owned specialty pharmacy location alongside contract pharmacies, automate 340B ESP claims-data uploads to unlock restricted NDCs, and enforce strict EHR encounter gates; id: wotc_hourly_payroll_tax_credit_contingency_engine; track id: track_1; name: Automated Form 8850 WOTC (Work Opportunity Tax Credit) & Section 41 R&D Contingency Engine; mechanism: Automate employer-authorized WOTC screening and separately substantiate Section 41 research credits, earning outcome-linked service fees only where permitted; program authorization, qualifying activities, wage coordination, and professional fee restrictions govern each claim.; inputs: Consented hiring records, Form 8850 responses, and payroll hours; Research project evidence and qualified expense ledgers; State workforce certification procedures and tax-year credit and fee rules; workflow: 1. Confirm WOTC authorization for each hire date and complete required prescreening by the job-offer date; 2. Submit Form 8850 and required supporting forms within the applicable 28-day deadline and track state certification and qualifying hours; 3. Separately document Section 41 qualifying research and expenses, reconciling wage overlap and applicable deduction adjustments with a tax professional; 4. Obtain employer and preparer approval before filing, retain audit support, and collect permitted fees without guaranteeing credits; metrics: Timely WOTC certification submission rate; Substantiated credits realized by the employer; Net permitted service fees after review and filing costs; platform risks: failure mode: Credit denial or impermissible contingent-fee arrangement; trigger: Expired program authority, late certification, unsupported research expenses, or restricted practitioner compensation; impact: Reduced credits, amended returns, penalties, and fee repayment exposure; detection metric: Deadline exceptions, certification denials, and unsupported expense share; fallback: Exclude unsupported claims and use compliant fixed-fee payroll and research-documentation services under independent tax review; id: sec_edgar_8k_vendor_trigger_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: SEC Form 8-K, Form D & C-Suite Turnover Trigger Arbitrage; mechanism: Parse SEC EDGAR real-time RSS/JSON feeds for Form D (private Reg D capital raises) and Form 8-K (Item 5.02 C-suite departures, Item 1.01 material agreements, Item 2.01 M&A closings) to trigger sub-hour executive outreach before commercial databases update.; inputs: SEC EDGAR real-time Submissions API & Form D / Form 8-K XML feeds; Automated filing parser extracting raise amounts, executive names, & signatory contacts; Enterprise recruiting, specialty finance, & B2B agency deal-routing desk; workflow: Ingest SEC EDGAR filings within seconds of publication using a compliant User-Agent header (<=10 requests/second); Extract Form D issuers raising $2M–$50M (who immediately deploy capital on hiring, growth agencies, and software) and Form 8-K executive transitions; Deliver tailored briefings to the filing officers and route warm introductions to executive search firms, enterprise software resellers, and B2B agencies; metrics: EDGAR publication-to-enrichment latency (seconds); Form D / 8-K executive response rate vs. cold baseline (3–5x lift); Retainer and placement referral fees generated per 100 filings; platform risks: failure mode: SEC EDGAR automated-access block or Reg D general-solicitation confusion; trigger: Exceeding SEC EDGAR's 10-requests-per-second fair-access limit or omitting the mandatory contact User-Agent header; impact: Temporary IP block by Akamai/SEC infrastructure; detection metric: Request rate strictly <=5 req/sec with compliant User-Agent and zero HTTP 403 responses; fallback: Enforce token-bucket rate limiting at 5 req/sec and mirror SEC nightly bulk zip archives for historical lookbacks; id: public_record_api_intelligence; track id: track_1; name: Public-Record & API Intelligence; mechanism: Ingest fragmented county dockets, probate registries, unclaimed property ledgers, and public APIs to surface uncontested claims or high-intent B2B triggers before manual competitors.; inputs: Court & probate dockets; State controller ledgers; Public licensing & entity APIs; workflow: Poll and normalize county/state record releases on an automated cadence; Cross-match entity/kinship/lien records and filter by minimum net fee threshold; Route verified dossiers into compliant outreach and claim execution; metrics: Cost per verified lead; Docket-to-contact latency (hours); Net recovery / conversion rate; platform risks: failure mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating; trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals; impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry; detection metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta; fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues; id: saas_technographic_churn_pixel_scraping; track id: track_1; name: DNS/Script Technographic Drop-Off & Renewal-Window Interception; mechanism: Crawl target commercial domains and DNS TXT/CNAME records weekly to detect the exact day a company installs or removes high-ticket enterprise software tags (Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Segment, NetSuite), predicting annual renewal windows (Month 10–11) and active vendor migrations.; inputs: Weekly HTTP script-tag, DOM header, & DNS TXT/CNAME technographic crawler; Historical install-timestamp ledger (calculating 12-month contract renewal windows); B2B executive contact graph & migration-agency/SaaS partner routing; workflow: Scan 500,000+ target B2B domains weekly for JavaScript SDKs, tracking pixels, and SPF/CNAME records of $20k–$150k/yr SaaS platforms; Flag accounts entering Month 10 of their annual contract (60 days before auto-renewal lock-in) or accounts running dual competing tags during a live evaluation; Route renewal-window and active-churn signals to competing SaaS sales teams, software resellers, and implementation agencies; metrics: Install/drop detection precision (%) and renewal-date accuracy; Outbound reply-to-demo conversion rate on Month-10 renewal targets; Per-opportunity bounty or retainer revenue per agency/SaaS partner; platform risks: failure mode: WAF/Cloudflare bot-blocking or false-positive tag detection from server-side GTM; trigger: High-concurrency crawling from datacenter IPs or misinterpreting server-side tag manager consolidation as vendor churn; impact: Incomplete technographic diffs or wasted sales outreach on false churn signals; detection metric: Crawler HTTP 200 success rate and multi-signal verification (DNS SPF/CNAME + careers-page job-posting confirmation); fallback: Combine passive DNS TXT/CNAME monitoring with job-posting technographic mentions to confirm true vendor switches before routing; id: multi_inbox_free_workspace_outbound_clusters; track id: track_2; name: Subsidized / Developer-Tenant Multi-Inbox Cold Outbound Infrastructure; mechanism: Provisioning hundreds of isolated secondary domains across subsidized Microsoft 365 developer/partner tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing, and low-cost SMTP relays—sending strictly 15–25 plain-text emails per inbox per day across 300+ free/subsidized mailboxes to deliver 150,000+ monthly B2B cold emails into primary inboxes without paying $6–$12/seat retail Google Workspace pricing.; inputs: Lookalike secondary domain portfolio with automated SPF, DKIM (2048-bit), DMARC (`p=quarantine`/`reject`), and custom tracking-free MX records; Subsidized M365 partner/developer tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing catch-alls, and distributed SMTP sending nodes; Automated peer-to-peer warmup network and master unibox reply-routing webhook; workflow: Provision 100–300 secondary sending domains and bind 2–3 mailboxes per domain via automated DNS and tenant scripts; Warm every mailbox for 14–21 days with realistic thread-depth conversations before introducing live outbound prospects; Cap daily outbound volume at <=20 zero-link, zero-tracking-pixel plain-text messages per mailbox per day to stay completely beneath ESP volume heuristics; Aggregate all prospect replies into a single unified AI-triaged inbox that books qualified B2B sales calls on pay-per-show or retainer terms; metrics: Primary-inbox placement rate (%) across Gmail and Microsoft 365 seed tests; All-in monthly infrastructure cost per 10,000 delivered plain-text emails ($); Positive reply rate (%) and booked meetings per 1,000 prospects contacted; platform risks: failure mode: Tenant-wide outbound throttling or domain-footprint blacklisting (Spamhaus DBL); trigger: Placing too many domains inside a single tenant, embedding tracking pixels, or exceeding 30 sends/day per mailbox; impact: Tenant suspension or domain-level spam-folder routing; detection metric: Daily seed-list inbox placement (%) and bounce rate (<1.5% hard threshold); fallback: Enforce max 2–3 domains per tenant, strip all open/click tracking pixels, verify 100% of leads via SMTP catch-all checks before sending, and keep hot-standby warmed domains ready for instant swap; id: high_velocity_dm_outbound_systems; track id: track_2; name: High-Velocity DM Outbound & Trigger Funnels; mechanism: Replace blind cold mass-DM blasts (which die to PeerFloodError and silent Message Request graveyards) with high-velocity comment-to-DM triggers, hand-raiser reaction hooks, and multi-inbox warm signal routing.; inputs: Short-form / community trigger posts ('Comment KEYWORD'); Signal-verified prospect handles; Automated DM qualification & booking bridge; workflow: Publish high-curiosity teardown or resource posts where prospects comment a trigger keyword or react to unlock a playbook or calculator; Deliver instant automated DM replies to warm hand-raisers (bypassing cold-DM filters because the user initiated interaction) or send contextual 1-to-1 DMs referencing an active public request; Qualify budget and timeline inside a 3-message DM micro-funnel and transition immediately to a booked call, checkout link, or owned SMS/email list; metrics: Trigger-comment to DM delivery rate; DM reply-to-qualified-conversation %; Revenue per 100 DM threads; platform risks: failure mode: PeerFloodError, shadow-filtering into 'Hidden Requests', or link-domain blacklisting; trigger: Sending identical unsolicited cold DMs with raw external URLs across freshly registered or SIM-farmed accounts; impact: Near-0% inbox placement, outbound DM block, or permanent account suspension; detection metric: Seen/reply ratio below 10% and outbound PeerFloodError / action-block frequency; fallback: Require user-initiated trigger action (comment/reaction/inbound message) before automated DM dispatch and send external links only after the prospect replies; id: private_b2b_gpo_umbrella_rebate_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: Private B2B Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) Umbrella & Contingent Spend-Audit Arbitrage; mechanism: Pool 10,000–75,000+ seats and indirect corporate spend across hundreds of SMB member companies under authorized master GPO volume brackets through Una, OMNIA or private vertical SaaS, parcel and telecom GPOs. Pair negotiated brackets with quarter-end vendor price-floor benchmarking informed by Vendr/Tropic playbooks, targeting 3%–12% vendor-paid administrative rebates and 25%–35% contingent Year-1 shared-savings splits under no savings, no fee agreements. Eligibility, rebate bases and benchmark access must be verified; disclose dual compensation and avoid double-counting rebates in client savings.; inputs: Executed GPO member and supplier agreements defining eligible aggregated spend, volume brackets, administrative rebates and compensation disclosures; Member-authorized invoices and seat inventories plus lawfully obtained, like-for-like Vendr/Tropic-style pricing benchmarks; Contingent audit contracts defining the Year-1 savings baseline, exclusions, 25%–35% fee schedule and independent reconciliation rights; workflow: 1. Enroll eligible SMB members with written authority and aggregate verified seat demand and indirect spend without exchanging competitively sensitive data.; 2. Validate GPO purchasing eligibility and negotiate supplier volume brackets using lawful quarter-end benchmarks for comparable service and commitment terms.; 3. Present disclosed vendor rebates and contingent fees, secure member approval and implement authorized contract changes against an agreed savings baseline.; 4. Reconcile actual Year-1 savings and vendor rebates, charge only earned shared-savings fees and audit bracket eligibility and renewal pricing.; metrics: Verified eligible seats and annual member spend within contracted GPO brackets; Realized Year-1 member savings net of contingent fees on a normalized baseline; Collected administrative rebates and shared-savings fees net of reversals; platform risks: failure mode: Ineligible pooled spend or disputed savings invalidates rebates and contingent fees; trigger: Supplier audit, volume-bracket shortfall, undisclosed dual compensation or an unsupported baseline adjustment; impact: Rebate clawbacks, member fee disputes and loss of supplier access; detection metric: Unsupported eligible spend and disputed savings or rebates as a percentage of billed compensation; fallback: Suspend disputed fees, reconcile documented baselines with members and suppliers, refund unearned amounts and move affected members to eligible purchasing agreements; platform risks: detection metric: Adverse-scenario funding gap, claims-to-budget variance, unrecovered stop-loss balances and unexplained differences between disclosed and received compensation.; failure mode: The proposed unbundled plan produces adverse claims exposure or undisclosed compensation despite appearing cheaper on headline premiums.; fallback: Retain or competitively rebid the existing structure when risk-adjusted economics are unfavorable, obtain explicit pricing fallbacks and narrow the engagement to disclosed advisory work until implementation conditions are satisfied.; impact: Employer costs exceed projections, coverage continuity deteriorates and advisory fees or the BOR relationship become disputed.; trigger: Incomplete claims data, stop-loss lasers or exclusions, nonrefundable captive collateral, ambiguous PBM rebate definitions or unsupported NADAC pricing for uncovered products.; track id: track_1; failure mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating; trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals; impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry; detection metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta; fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues; play id: public_record_api_intelligence; play name: Public-Record & API Intelligence; track id: track_1; failure mode: WAF/Cloudflare bot-blocking or false-positive tag detection from server-side GTM; trigger: High-concurrency crawling from datacenter IPs or misinterpreting server-side tag manager consolidation as vendor churn; impact: Incomplete technographic diffs or wasted sales outreach on false churn signals; detection metric: Crawler HTTP 200 success rate and multi-signal verification (DNS SPF/CNAME + careers-page job-posting confirmation); fallback: Combine passive DNS TXT/CNAME monitoring with job-posting technographic mentions to confirm true vendor switches before routing; play id: saas_technographic_churn_pixel_scraping; play name: DNS/Script Technographic Drop-Off & Renewal-Window Interception; track id: track_1; failure mode: Tenant-wide outbound throttling or domain-footprint blacklisting (Spamhaus DBL); trigger: Placing too many domains inside a single tenant, embedding tracking pixels, or exceeding 30 sends/day per mailbox; impact: Tenant suspension or domain-level spam-folder routing; detection metric: Daily seed-list inbox placement (%) and bounce rate (<1.5% hard threshold); fallback: Enforce max 2–3 domains per tenant, strip all open/click tracking pixels, verify 100% of leads via SMTP catch-all checks before sending, and keep hot-standby warmed domains ready for instant swap; play id: multi_inbox_free_workspace_outbound_clusters; play name: Subsidized / Developer-Tenant Multi-Inbox Cold Outbound Infrastructure; track id: track_2; failure mode: PeerFloodError, shadow-filtering into 'Hidden Requests', or link-domain blacklisting; trigger: Sending identical unsolicited cold DMs with raw external URLs across freshly registered or SIM-farmed accounts; impact: Near-0% inbox placement, outbound DM block, or permanent account suspension; detection metric: Seen/reply ratio below 10% and outbound PeerFloodError / action-block frequency; fallback: Require user-initiated trigger action (comment/reaction/inbound message) before automated DM dispatch and send external links only after the prospect replies; play id: high_velocity_dm_outbound_systems; play name: High-Velocity DM Outbound & Trigger Funnels; track id: track_2; failure mode: Ineligible pooled spend or disputed savings invalidates rebates and contingent fees; trigger: Supplier audit, volume-bracket shortfall, undisclosed dual compensation or an unsupported baseline adjustment; impact: Rebate clawbacks, member fee disputes and loss of supplier access; detection metric: Unsupported eligible spend and disputed savings or rebates as a percentage of billed compensation; fallback: Suspend disputed fees, reconcile documented baselines with members and suppliers, refund unearned amounts and move affected members to eligible purchasing agreements; play id: private_b2b_gpo_umbrella_rebate_arbitrage;
